Render a basemap view

Source: R/basemap.R
render_png.Rd

  • render_png() writes or returns a PNG.

  • render_svg() writes or returns a vector SVG document (width x height user units; pixel_ratio does not apply).

  • render_array() returns an integer array [height, width, 4] (RGBA, 0–255) with the extent as attributes, like render_basemap_raw().

  • render_raster() (R only) returns a terra::rast() (EPSG:3857, layers red, green, blue, alpha).

Usage

render_png(m, path = NULL)

render_svg(
  m,
  path = NULL,
  text = c("editable", "bitmap", "paths"),
  embed_fonts = c("subset", "full", "none"),
  font_dirs = NULL
)

render_array(m)

render_raster(m)

Arguments

m

A basemap() object.

path

Output file, or NULL to return the result.

text

For render_svg(): "editable" writes labels as <text> elements (editable, selectable) at MapLibre's glyph positions, halos as strokes, with the style's fonts embedded, and falls back to "bitmap" for labels whose font file is not available; "bitmap" draws every label from the style's own glyph bitmaps, thresholded by SVG filters as MapLibre's shader does (MapLibre's look at any zoom, not editable); "paths" writes glyph outlines traced from those bitmaps (plain paths).

embed_fonts

For render_svg(): "subset" (only the glyphs used), "full" (whole fonts, for retyping labels) or "none" (fonts by name only). Fonts come from font_dirs, the BASEMAPPER_FONT_DIRS folders, a local cache, then Google Fonts for open fonts; others are referenced by name.

font_dirs

For render_svg(): folders of .ttf / .otf files to use first.

Value

render_png(): the PNG as a raw vector (invisibly when written). render_svg(): the SVG as a string (invisibly when written).

Details

Image sizes are width * pixel_ratio by height * pixel_ratio device pixels. Python: m.render_png(), m.render_svg(), m.render_array().
